title: Minimum Array Sum
statement:
Two kinds of operation can shrink the elements of the integer array `nums`:

- **Halve**: replace `nums[i]` by half its value, rounded up. At most `op1` elements may be halved, and no index more than once.
- **Subtract**: replace `nums[i]` by `nums[i] - k`, which is allowed only while `nums[i]` is at least `k`. At most `op2` elements may be reduced this way, and no index more than once.

The same index may receive both operations, one of each, in either order; the subtraction's condition is checked against the value at the moment it is applied. Return the smallest sum of `nums` that some choice of operations within these limits achieves (using none at all is allowed).
signature: int minArraySum(int[] nums, int k, int op1, int op2)
notes:
## Intuition

Each element ends up untouched, halved, reduced by `k`, or both. Only the two budgets link the elements, so a table indexed by the halvings and subtractions allowed captures everything; trying every assignment instead (the brute force) grows exponentially with the length of `nums`.

If one element `x` gets both operations, halving first is never worse: the subtraction then removes a full `k` rather than about `k / 2`. That order needs the halved value to be at least `k`; otherwise subtracting first still works whenever `x >= k`.

## Approach

1. `dp[a][b]` is the smallest sum of the elements placed so far using at most `a` halvings and `b` subtractions; it starts at 0 everywhere.
2. For each `x`, compute `half` (rounded up), `minus` and `both`, with `Infinity` for a choice that is not allowed.
3. Each cell takes the best of four choices: leave `x` (`dp[a][b] + x`), halve it (`dp[a - 1][b] + half`), subtract (`dp[a][b - 1] + minus`), or both (`dp[a - 1][b - 1] + both`).
4. `a` and `b` run downwards, so the cells read in step 3 still hold the sums from before `x` and one table is enough.
5. Return `dp[op1][op2]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`k = 3`, `op1 = op2 = 1`. The table after each element, as `dp[0][0] / dp[0][1] / dp[1][0] / dp[1][1]`:

| `x` | `half`, `minus`, `both` | table |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1, ∞, ∞ | 2 / 2 / 1 / 1 |
| 8 | 4, 5, 1 | 10 / 7 / 6 / 3 |
| 3 | 2, 0, 0 | 13 / 10 / 9 / 6 |
| 19 | 10, 16, 7 | 32 / 29 / 23 / 20 |
| 3 | 2, 0, 0 | 35 / 32 / 26 / 23 |

The answer is `dp[1][1] = 23`, for instance by halving 19 to 10 and subtracting 3 from 8.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · op1 · op2): each element updates every cell once.
- Space: O(op1 · op2) for the single table.

## Pitfalls

- Trying only one order for both operations: halving first gives 1 for `x = 8, k = 3`, but for `x = 9, k = 6` only subtracting first is allowed (9 → 3 → 2).
- Rounding the halving down: it rounds up, so half of 19 is 10 and half of 1 is still 1.
- Running the budgets upwards: a cell would then build on sums that already include `x`, counting it twice.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dp[a][b]` | least sum so far with at most `a` halvings and `b` subtractions |
| `x` | the element being placed |
| `half`, `minus`, `both` | `x` after halving, after subtracting, after both (`Infinity` if not allowed) |
| `a`, `b` | the halvings and subtractions the cell allows |
| `best` | best sum found for the current cell |

narration.5: Place the elements one at a time.
narration.6: Halving rounds up, so an odd value keeps its extra half.
narration.7: Subtracting k is allowed only when x is at least k; otherwise this choice is impossible.
narration.9: If the halved value is still at least k, halving first and then subtracting is the best way to use both.
narration.10: Halve, then remove a full k.
narration.11: Otherwise both still fit when x itself is at least k: subtract first, then halve.
narration.14: Budgets run downwards so the cells read below still hold the sums from before x.
narration.16: Choice 1: leave x as it is.
narration.18: Choice 2: halve x, spending one halving.
narration.21: Choice 3: subtract k from x, spending one subtraction.
narration.24: Choice 4: apply both operations to x, spending one of each.
narration.26: Keep the best of the choices for this pair of budgets.
narration.30: The full budgets give the answer.
